Command: The high priest shall not have relations with a widow even outside marriage
Summary: The command: The high priest shall not have relations with a widow even outside marriage (Leviticus 21:15). The prohibition reached beyond marriage itself: the high priest was not to profane his seed by relations with a widow.
Commandment: The high priest shall not have relations with a widow even outside marriage.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The marriage rules guarded the priesthood's public holiness in a world where priests were public figures; they are not Christian marriage law, which is governed by creation and by the New Testament household commands (Matthew 19:3-9; Ephesians 5:22-33). The high priest's stricter rule — a virgin of his own people — is included here as the second half of the same law.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: for he is holy unto his God (Leviticus 21:7-8).
Function: The prohibition reached beyond marriage itself: the high priest was not to profane his seed by relations with a widow — a ceremonial law that closed the back door. Its goal was to guard the high priest's seed with the same strictness as his marriage, so the rule could not be dodged outside the wedding. The evil was profaning the holiest household by a liaison the marriage law did not cover. It restrained that by extending the ban past marriage: the widow was off limits in every way.
